proof: A unique monotonic claim token identifies the currently owned copy; stale local tokens are discarded when Redis no longer contains the claim.
Processed signal identity remains durable and successful claims are acknowledged only after execution or an accepted fail-closed outcome.
Claim, ack, nack, DLQ transfer, and expired reclaim use atomic Lua state transitions.
A crash-before-ack signal becomes reclaimable after its visibility deadline, while a live unexpired claim cannot be stolen.
Validation and execution exceptions are durably dead-lettered; a failed DLQ transfer does not mark the signal processed.
Binding, runtime, and capital-pool identity is checked before execution and retained in binding-scoped pending, claim, and DLQ state.
Capital mutation bodies are rebound to verified service, actor, role, and tenant claims before endpoint logic executes.
Six crashed OS processes recover exactly their own six binding-scoped Redis claims after restart, with no pending, in-flight, or DLQ residue.
Two spawned reconcilers converge to one Redis-fenced leader; after expiry the successor receives a higher token and the stale predecessor cannot renew.
Nack atomically returns an owned claim to pending; terminal failure atomically transfers it to the scoped DLQ.
Leader demotion stops local worker mutations, and every worker spawn or termination requires current fence validation.
